title: Units, prefixes and conversions
summary: SI prefixes, squared and cubed units, eV ↔ J, nm ↔ m, mA/cm² ↔ A/m²: the conversions behind most lost exam points.

diagrams.title: Unit converter with the reasoning shown
diagrams.tryThis: Convert 1 cm² to m², then 1 cm⁻³ to m⁻³: watch how the exponent of the prefix is multiplied by the power of the unit.

checks.prompt: A photon has an energy of 2.5 eV. What is its energy in joules?
hints: 1 eV is the energy one elementary charge gains across 1 V.

checks.prompt: A solar cell delivers 12 mA/cm². Express this in A/m².
hints: Convert the numerator and the denominator separately.
1 mA = 10⁻³ A and 1 cm² = (10⁻² m)² = 10⁻⁴ m².

checks.prompt: Carrier densities in week 2 are given per cm³. How many per m³ is $10^{16}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$?

options.feedback: Correct: 1 m³ = 10⁶ cm³, so a density per m³ is 10⁶ times larger.
That divides by 10⁶. A cubic metre holds a million cubic centimetres, so it contains *more* particles.
You used 10² (cm → m) without cubing it. Volumes cube the factor: (10²)³ = 10⁶.
That divides by 10² instead of multiplying by 10⁶.

hints: How many cm³ fit in one m³?
A density is ‘per volume’: more volume → more particles.
